newsitem.title: USA: Italy Dini sees interest rates falling.
newsitem.headline: Italy Dini sees interest rates falling.

text.p: Official Italian interest rates are set to continue their descent but the timing of a move by the Bank of Italy remains unclear, Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Saturday.
"All central banks are resistent and have conservative and cautious thinking," Dini told reporters. "The moment will come when official interest rates will also come down," he added.
"We respect the judgment of our governor but I am of the view that interest rates will come down along with declining inflation and the improving conditions of our economy," he added.
Italy's inflation, which according to preliminary CPI data released on Friday is running at 1.5 percent year-on-year, is at its lowest level since the late 1960s.
Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio has held the official discount rate at 6.75 percent since January, arguing that he is not yet convinced that inflation has been well and truly beaten.
The governor is holding out for lower interest rates which would help lower the cost of servicing a crushing national debt burden and boost a languishing economy.
